records.issue_text: Removing the last member of the final page strands the UI on an empty page: after a successful removal, findMembers() re-fetches with the unchanged offset, so if the removed member was the only one on the last page the refetch returns an empty list and the admin is left on an empty page until manually clicking previous; offset should be re-clamped against the new total after deletion
records.rationale: Verified mechanism in the diff: model.removeMember calls self.findMembers() after DELETE, and findMembers uses this.get('offset') unchanged; nothing re-clamps offset to the new user_count after removal. If the removed member was the sole one on the last page, the refetch offsets past the end, returning an empty member list with currentPage > totalPages, stranding the UI on an empty page.

records.issue_text: Server members endpoint has unbounded limit with no upper clamp (a client can pass limit=10000000 to force full-group serialization, a repeatable resource-exhaustion vector on a non-admin endpoint), and neither limit nor offset is validated as non-negative — negative values pass into LIMIT/OFFSET -1, which PostgreSQL rejects, producing an unhandled ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid → 500 instead of a 400
records.rationale: The diff adds `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` in the public groups_controller#members with no upper clamp or non-negative validation, then passes them directly into `.limit(limit).offset(offset)`. A client-controlled unbounded limit on a non-admin endpoint is a real resource-exhaustion concern, and negative values would raise an unhandled AR error (PostgreSQL rejects negative LIMIT/OFFSET). Verifiable mechanism in the diff; the exact 500-vs-400 behavior depends on unseen error handling, so slightly hedged.

records.issue_text: Stale usernames carried across groups: usernames is a plain controller property on the reused adminGroup controller and setupController never resets it, so pending usernames typed for group A persist when navigating to group B and clicking 'Add' inserts them into the wrong group; addMembers also never clears the input after a successful add, so a second click re-submits the same list
records.rationale: The diff sets `usernames: null` on the controller but the new setupController only does `controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();` — it never resets usernames. The addMembers action even carries a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment and calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` without clearing, so stale usernames persist and could be added to a different group. Mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

records.rationale: The diff adds tests like `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "l77t"` and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` and `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, name: "WAT"` which assume group id 1 is a seeded automatic group, while other tests in the same file explicitly use `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` (e.g. the .destroy 422 test). This reliance on implicit seed data instead of fabricated fixtures is a specific, substantive test-brittleness concern grounded in the diff, not a behavioral bug.

records.issue_text: Unbounded limit on the public members endpoint: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no ceiling (old code capped automatic groups at 200), so limit=1000000 serializes the full membership of any visible group in one request — a mass user enumeration and DoS vector; also offset=-1 passes straight through to SQL (OFFSET -1) causing a 500
records.rationale: The diff shows `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` passed directly to `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping, so an attacker-controlled huge limit serializes the entire membership in one request and a negative offset reaches SQL as OFFSET -1, likely causing a 500. The mechanism is verifiable in the new members controller code; whether surrounding middleware prevents it is unknown, so moderate confidence.

records.issue_text: Uncapped limit/offset on the group members endpoint in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb allows any caller (including anonymous users on visible groups) to force full materialization/serialization of a group's entire membership via ?limit=999999999 or force Postgres to walk/sort and discard the entire member set via ?offset=1000000000; clamp both values (e.g., using Discourse's page_params helper) and reject non-positive values
records.rationale: The diff shows app/controllers/groups_controller.rb `members` uses `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` with no clamping — an uncapped limit would serialize the full membership and a huge offset forces a full walk/sort/discard. Unlike pre-diff code, this now publicly exposes arbitrary limit/offset to all callers (previously pagination was only honored for automatic groups). The mechanism is verifiable in the diff, but it is a robustness/DoS-hardening concern rather than a clear functional defect, so it fits important_non_bug.
